checklistCore.fiqhPosture: Oman-facing, Ibadi-aware, fiqh-pluralist, governed through qualified fiqh al-muamalat Sharia Supervisory Board review
checklistCore.product: banked Sukuk-backed stablecoin plus optional halal DeFi service-fee rails

items.title: Appoint an Omani-facing Sharia Supervisory Board
items.gate: Board must include scholars competent in fiqh al-muamalat and at least one member able to address Omani/Ibadi sensitivities, while respecting Oman fiqh pluralism.
items.evidence: Signed SSB appointment letters, CVs, conflict checks, fit-and-proper review, meeting calendar.

items.title: Obtain product fatwa before public launch
items.gate: Fatwa must cover stablecoin issuance, reserve policy, redemption, TAP pledge, Lightning routing service fees, TradeLayer arb mandate, purification, and insolvency waterfall.
items.evidence: Product fatwa, term sheet reviewed by SSB, Sharia issue log.

items.title: Map escalation to CBO High Sharia Supervisory Authority
items.gate: Any point of market-wide uncertainty should be pre-cleared or escalated through the Islamic banking sponsor or counsel.
items.evidence: Escalation memo, regulator Q&A, board minutes.

items.title: Create internal Sharia compliance office
items.gate: Compliance must review every reserve asset, token contract change, fee formula, and DeFi mandate before activation.
items.evidence: Policy manual, approval workflow, release checklist, audit trail.

items.title: Keep stablecoin principal separate from yield products
items.gate: Holding the stablecoin must not grant portfolio yield, interest, or guaranteed investment return.
items.evidence: Token terms, user disclosures, accounting ledger, smart-contract config.

items.title: Use Islamic bank custody and segregated accounts
items.gate: Reserve cash and Sukuk assets must be held through approved Islamic banking/custody arrangements, segregated from operating capital.
items.evidence: Account agreements, custody statements, board-approved signatory matrix.

items.title: Screen each Sukuk issue individually
items.gate: Each Sukuk must pass asset, issuer, use-of-proceeds, purchase-undertaking, liquidity, tradability, late-payment, and purification review.
items.evidence: Sukuk screening memo, prospectus extract, Sharia certificate, SSB approval.

items.title: Maintain par-redemption liquidity buffer
items.gate: Eligible reserve value after haircuts must exceed minted stablecoin units, with a board-approved redemption buffer.
items.evidence: Daily reserve report, haircut model, auditor tie-out, liquidity stress test.

items.title: Disable farm REIT backing until separately approved
items.gate: Farm REIT exposure may be a future yield vault, but it must not back the stablecoin until appraised, tokenized, liquid, and Sharia-approved.
items.evidence: Blocked-asset register, future product memo, separate propertyId plan.

items.title: One reserve unit, one issued unit accounting
items.gate: Minting must be tied to reserve evidence; burns must reduce outstanding supply or release reserve claims.
items.evidence: Mint/burn ledger, reserve proof hash, auditor reconciliation.

items.title: No rehypothecation of pledged stablecoin
items.gate: A stablecoin unit pledged into TAP/Lightning or TradeLayer arb cannot simultaneously support another active mandate.
items.evidence: UTXORef allocation proof, propertyId ledger, duplicate-pledge rejection tests.

items.title: Separate service-fee revenue from stablecoin principal
items.gate: Routing fees, arb profits, and operator fees must be booked as service revenue events, not stablecoin reserve yield.
items.evidence: Service-fee ledger, revenue event hashes, user disclosures.

items.title: Publish proof-of-reserve without leaking bank secrets
items.gate: Investor-facing proof should bind reserve totals and eligible assets while protecting account numbers and counterparties where needed.
items.evidence: Merkle proof design, auditor attestation, redaction policy.

items.title: Classify Lightning hawala-style fees as ujrah/service fees
items.gate: Dynamic fees must be compensation for routing, settlement, compliance, and liquidity service actually provided, not time value of money.
items.evidence: Fee formula, route logs, service evidence, SSB approval.

items.title: Confirm qabd or constructive possession for TAP pledges
items.gate: The system must prove control or constructive possession before sale, pledge, routing, or settlement of the tokenized asset.
items.evidence: TAP proof, lock event, custody attestation, transfer proof.

items.title: Ban leverage, lending, shorting, and guaranteed arb return
items.gate: TradeLayer arb must be spot, funded, bounded, non-borrowed, non-margin, and limited to approved assets and venues.
items.evidence: Arb mandate, venue whitelist, risk limits, execution logs.

items.title: Reduce gharar and maysir in algorithmic routing
items.gate: Routing and arb algorithms must expose fee formula, failure modes, slippage limits, and kill switches; no lottery-like payoff structures.
items.evidence: Algorithm spec, scenario tests, risk disclosures, monitoring dashboard.

items.title: Get CBO/payment-system legal classification
items.gate: Do not launch public stablecoin transfer or redemption until counsel confirms CBO perimeter, licensing, bank sponsorship, and payment-service treatment.
items.evidence: CBO legal memo, sponsor-bank approval, no-objection or license path.

items.title: Get FSA/securities classification for Sukuk and vaults
items.gate: Sukuk reserve holding, yield vaults, REIT sleeves, and private placement must be classified under FSA/capital-market rules before fundraising.
items.evidence: FSA legal memo, offering exemption memo, private-placement docs.

items.title: Implement AML/CFT and sanctions controls before minting
items.gate: Banked stablecoin users, redemptions, corridors, and DeFi mandates require onboarding, monitoring, screening, and suspicious activity escalation.
items.evidence: AML policy, vendor contract, transaction monitoring rules, staff training.

items.title: Run closed pilot before public fundraising
items.gate: Launch sequence should be sandbox/private pilot, audited reserve proof, Sharia audit, then limited raise.
items.evidence: Pilot report, audit report, Sharia audit certificate, board go/no-go.

launchPlan.title: Scholar and regulator preflight
launchPlan.deliverable: SSB appointment, Omani/Ibadi fiqh memo, CBO/FSA perimeter memo, product fatwa scope

launchPlan.title: Reserve and SPV setup
launchPlan.deliverable: Islamic bank accounts, custody agreement, Sukuk whitelist, reserve policy, redemption waterfall

launchPlan.title: TradeLayer stablecoin dry run
launchPlan.deliverable: Mint/burn ledger, proof-of-reserve hash, redemption simulation, no-yield stablecoin terms

launchPlan.title: Halal DeFi closed pilot
launchPlan.deliverable: TAP pledge, Lightning service-fee route, TradeLayer spot arb mandate, non-rehypothecation proof

launchPlan.title: Audit and Sharia certification
launchPlan.deliverable: External audit, Sharia audit, incident runbook, board approval

launchPlan.title: Private placement / limited launch
launchPlan.deliverable: Qualified investor docs, banking sponsor signoff, capped issuance, daily reserve publication

launchPlan.title: Scale to Sukuk and farm REIT modules
launchPlan.deliverable: Separate propertyIds for yield vaults, REIT appraisals, income proof, liquidity gates

stopConditions: No named Sharia Supervisory Board and product fatwa.
No CBO/payment perimeter memo for stablecoin issuance and redemption.
No FSA/securities memo for Sukuk reserve handling and fundraising.
Any stablecoin holder entitlement to reserve yield.
Any use of conventional interest-bearing accounts as reserve assets without purification and board approval.
Any DeFi route using leverage, borrowing, lending, shorting, or guaranteed return language.
Any farm REIT asset counted toward stablecoin backing before separate approval.

sources.title: Oman Foreign Ministry: Religious freedom and fiqh pluralism
sources.note: Oman states that most Omanis belong to the Ibadi school, recognizes multiple fiqh schools, and states that Islamic Shariah is the basis of legislation.

sources.title: Central Bank of Oman: Legal Framework for Islamic Banking
sources.note: CBO materials describe Sharia Supervisory Boards for licensed Islamic banking entities and a High Sharia Supervisory Authority for the Central Bank.

sources.title: Central Bank of Oman: Islamic Banking Regulatory Framework
sources.note: CBO describes the Islamic Banking Regulatory Framework as including licensing rules, guidance, and Sharia governance for Islamic banking operations.

sources.title: Oman Financial Services Authority: Bonds and Sukuk Regulation announcement
sources.note: FSA announced the 2024 Bonds and Sukuk Regulation, including issuance, private placement, SPVs, financial trusts, Sharia compliance, agents, disclosures, and green/sustainable Sukuk.

sources.title: Central Bank of Oman: Virtual Assets and VASPs circular
sources.note: CBO circulars and notices emphasize virtual asset risk, AML/CFT exposure, and enhanced due diligence expectations for licensed institutions.
